items.t: Said the latest federal executive order on elections was overreaching.
items.q: Secretary Steve Hobbs’ Statement Regarding Latest Overreaching Federal Executive Order On Elections

record.t: Was sworn in as President of the National Association of Secretaries of State (NASS) on July 17 at the close of its 2026 Summer Conference.
record.q: Hobbs was sworn in July 17 at the conclusion of the NASS 2026 Summer Conference in Rapid City, South Dakota.

record.t: Was appointed by Gov. Jay Inslee to replace Kim Wyman as Washington Secretary of State.
record.q: Hobbs was appointed by Democratic Gov. Jay Inslee last November to replace Republican Secretary of State Kim Wyman once she took a key election security job in the Biden administration.

record.t: Has served as Washington's 16th Secretary of State since 2021.
record.q: Hobbs is Washington’s 16th Secretary of State and has served in the role since 2021.

record.t: Represented Washington's 44th Legislative District in the state Senate before becoming Secretary of State.
record.q: Before becoming Secretary of State, he represented Washington’s 44th Legislative District in the state Senate.

record.t: Was elected Secretary of State, the first elected Democrat in the office in nearly six decades.
record.q: It’s official: Steve Hobbs is the first elected Democrat in Washington state to serve as secretary of state in nearly six decades.

record.t: Served on the NASS Executive Board and co-chaired NASS committees.
record.q: Hobbs has been an active leader within NASS, serving on the Executive Board, co-chairing NASS committees, and showcasing Washington’s efforts to strengthen election security

record.t: Pushed back against a Justice Department claim of more than 400 noncitizens registered to vote in Washington, saying the state's review of the list found deficiencies.
record.q: Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs pushed back against the findings, saying the state’s review of the list uncovered "several glaring deficiencies.
